verdict.line: You win if you deny Nasus's Siphoning Strike stacks and force all-ins before level 6; you lose if the lane stalls and he free-farms into a split-push monster with Fury of the Sands up.

brief.thesis: Nasus's Q (Siphoning Strike) permanently buffs its own damage every time it kills a minion, so every creep he takes uncontested compounds forever — this is the entire reason the matchup sits at an even 53.2% instead of a blowout. Illaoi's W (Harsh Lesson) is a 4-second-cooldown leap with no cast time or skillshot component, which lets her punish Nasus's short 255-range, immobile kit far more often than he can punish her back. OP.GG's own read confirms it: Illaoi has the lane and solo-kill edge early-mid, and the matchup only evens out once Nasus has banked enough Q stacks and his ultimate comes online.

theirWindow.what: Wither decelerates your Movement and Attack Speed on a 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown — do not commit your W (Harsh Lesson) all-in while it's up, since he can kite the slow into a bad trade or lock you down for teammates. Bait it out or wait for the cooldown before diving.

yourWindow.what: Use W (Harsh Lesson) on cooldown to leap onto Nasus whenever he reaches for a Siphoning Strike last-hit — the leap also pulls nearby Tentacles onto him, so every trade both denies a stack and heals you through the passive. This is the window OP.GG flags as Illaoi-favored; spend it.

R (Leap of Faith) online, his R weak

start.why: Highest-played start into this matchup (74% pick, 51.9% WR over 108 games) — the lifesteal lets you win the W-leap trade war without losing the sustain race to his Soul Eater passive.

boots.why: 60.9% pick, 54.3% WR — Nasus's entire kit (auto-attacks, Siphoning Strike, and his drained Fury of the Sands damage) is physical and auto-reliant, so flat auto-attack reduction directly blunts his stacking damage.

core.why: First item in the highest-performing path (80% WR over 25 games) — the armor shred stacks with your repeated W leaps to push through his growing resistances as his stacks climb.
Second in that same path — the slow-on-hit from the proc locks Nasus in place for follow-up Tentacle swings, countering his lack of a built-in escape.
Closes the top path (80% WR, 22.5% pick) — the shield and tenacity-adjacent survivability let you commit to all-ins without dying to his Spirit Fire armor shred poke.

situational.when: the game goes long and his stacked Q autos start threatening burst through your shield
his Soul Eater lifesteal and Fury of the Sands health drain are keeping him alive through your all-ins
he's stacked enough Q that his autos alone are winning extended trades

runes.keystoneWhy: 55.9% WR, 39.9% pick — Grasp's proc rewards the repeated short trades your W leap creates, and the permanent health growth offsets Nasus's long-game scaling instead of racing a burst keystone you don't need this early.

summoners.why: Highest played combo at 59.9% pick (54.5% WR) — Teleport lets you reset back to lane after winning an all-in trade or capitalize on your early lead by joining skirmishes elsewhere before Nasus's stacks catch up.

playing.title: Leap on every stack attempt
playing.detail: W (Harsh Lesson) is up every 4 seconds — use it to punish Nasus whenever he commits to a Siphoning Strike last-hit, since denying the stack matters more than the trade damage itself.

playing.title: Force the Vessel decision
playing.detail: E (Test of Spirit) at 900 range strips his spirit and echoes damage back to him; if he can't kill the spirit or escape its range he becomes a Vessel that spawns Tentacles against him, so throw it before he can retreat.

playing.title: Bait Wither before all-in
playing.detail: Wither's 15-to-11s cooldown is his only way to stick to or peel off you — provoke it with a feinted trade, then commit your real all-in once it's down.

playing.title: Contest every last hit you can
playing.detail: Because Q stacks are permanent, a denied creep is worth more here than in a normal lane — prioritize trading on his CS attempts over your own farm when you have priority.

playing.title: Save ultimate for the kill, not the poke
playing.detail: R (Leap of Faith) is on a long 120/95/70/70/70s cooldown and spawns a Tentacle per champion hit — use it to close out an all-in you've already won, not to start a 50/50 trade.

playing.title: Don't facecheck past level 15
playing.detail: Once he's banked enough Q stacks and has Fury of the Sands up, a 1v1 you were winning at level 6 can flip instantly from his health drain — play around vision and teammates instead of dueling blind.

brief.patchCaveat: Every item, rune, and summoner spell above comes from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the win rates, pick rates, and sample sizes are real. The mechanical reasoning — why the W leap punishes him, why Q stacks compound, why the powercurve shifts late — is my own tactical read, not sourced data.

stats.opponentTip: Harass Nasus while laning to prevent him from gaining stacks through (Q). Illaoi has the upper hand during early and mid-game, so use this to your advantage to engage when possible.
